about.title: Saratoga Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Saratoga's collision counts tell a quiet but real story: 61 injury crashes and 72 people hurt in the most recent final reporting year, with Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing the most activity. Corridors like Saratoga Avenue, SR-85, Saratoga Sunnyvale Road, and Saratoga Los Gatos Road see the heaviest traffic volume, and that's where a lot of these collisions happen. Whether you were rear-ended near a shopping center on Saratoga Avenue or caught in a merge issue on SR-85, the aftermath can be disorienting — medical appointments, insurance calls, missed work. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect Santa Clara County residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of a crash and explain options, all on a contingency basis so there's nothing owed upfront. The goal is to help you get oriented quickly, before evidence fades or deadlines slip by.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: Most car accident injury claims in California must be filed within two years, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can help identify which deadline applies to your situation.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning even if you're found partly responsible, you can still recover damages reduced by your share of fault. Insurers often use recorded statements to shift blame onto you early, so it helps to have guidance before speaking with them.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California doesn't limit compensation for pain and suffering in most car accident cases. That makes it worthwhile to have a full picture of your losses documented before accepting any settlement offer.

items.question: I was in a crash on Saratoga Avenue and the insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: It's usually best to hold off. Recorded statements to the other driver's insurer can be used to minimize your claim, especially under California's comparative fault rules. An independent attorney can talk to the insurer on your behalf instead.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Saratoga?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a government entity, like a city vehicle or a road maintenance issue, was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
